The account-face brief

Known by shape.
Drawn with personality.

The account design already has the right idea: a face you can pick out at a glance. This edition keeps every subject in the current deck and gives it the same heavy ink, off-centre eyes, paper cuts, and comic energy as After Hours.

The fox gets a sly wedge of a muzzle. The snail gets a big, lazy spiral. The cactus becomes a ribbed desert oddball. Each is an original drawing, with a second, simpler master for the smallest places a face appears.

03 / The drawing language

A family of misfits.

01

Recognize the subject.

The owl’s eye discs. The camel’s two humps. The panda’s patches. A clear anatomical or object cue comes before the joke.

02

Let the ink do it.

Unequal contours, deep black planes, blunt hatching, and little paper highlights give the drawings their retro print character.

03

Keep the paper white.

The cut edge stays white on both grounds. Color is unnecessary for telling these faces apart; their forms carry the identity.

Design & implementation notes

This is the proposed vector artwork for the current account-face deck, read from packages/contracts/src/user-face.ts. The comparison uses the shipping UserFaceView and the new shared FaceSticker leaf.

The deck, stored emoji, assignment, collision policy, per-user tilt, custom emoji entry, and coin frame remain with the existing account system. This catalogue does not change an account. Unknown emoji have no drawing in this pack and should keep the native renderer.

All 48 drawings are original vector interpretations. The emoji specimens use your system’s emoji font. The sticker artwork contains no emoji glyphs, Apple assets, traced Stink Dings paths, embedded fonts, or raster images.

Master boards: 112 units detailed, 56 units small. The artwork finish removes the outer die-cut edge; white interiors remain opaque. Export scale tests are a visual proof, not a substitute for testing recognition with people in the actual account picker.

The source is tooling/face-stickers/art.py. A deterministic generator checks exact deck coverage and builds SVGs, metadata, and the ZIP. Studio and this offline report use the same catalogue component.
